pr_title: Fix AltGr not working in the settings UI
pr_body:
Since the settings UI's input fields behave similarly to the terminal's input,
`TerminalPage::_KeyDownHandler` also needs to behave similarly to
`TermControl::_KeyHandler`. This commit copies all relevant code
over from the latter into the former, including the suppression
of AltGr keys for keychord/action handling.

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #11788
* [x] I work here
* [x] Tests added/passed

## Validation Steps Performed
* Use a German keyboard layout
* Open 2 regular tabs and 1 settings tab and focus an input field
* AltGr+2 produces the character ² ✔️
* Ctrl+Alt+2 opens the second tab ✔️
pr_comments: I've asked Mike about that and he mentioned that it's likely not worth the effort for now, considering that we should probably consolidate the entire input stack anyways. In my personal opinion a bit code duplication once in a while is fine if the offending code isn't that complex.

issue_context.title: Not possible to type dollar sign in settings
issue_context.body:
### Windows Terminal version

1.11.2921.0

### Windows build number

10.0.19044.1379

### Other Software

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

Open settings tab.
Try to type a $ in the Starting Directory field.
E.g. `\\wsl$\Ubuntu-18.04\home\user`

This happens with Swedish keyboard where you type $ by pressing AltGr+4.
This used to work with previous versions.


### Expected Behavior

A $ should be inserted at the cursor position.

### Actual Behavior

The right-most tab becomes active.
If the Settings tab is the right-most tab, nothing happens.
comments:
Interesting. This is probably caused by us looking in the keybindings even in the SUI now. I think this is the roughly same thing as #10349, which has a workaround in https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/10349#issuecomment-855963803. 

@lhecker double check me on that?
